keyword: how long is the moon mission

verifications.claim: The Artemis II moon mission is scheduled to last approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "their 10-day mission" (R1), "approximately 10-day Artemis II mission" (R2), "10 days" (R3), "overall mission around the Moon and back expected to take about 10 days" (R4), "next 10 days" (R5), "10-day journey" (R6), "10-day mission" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the mission duration as 10 days.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: All relevant references confirm the exact launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II has a four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts" (R1), "four crew members" (R2), "Four astronauts" (R3), "four Artemis II astronauts" (R5), "four astronauts" (R6), "crew of four astronauts" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as four astronauts across references.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will journey to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "lifting four astronauts toward space ... around the moon" (R1), "journey to deep space" ... "around the Moon" (R2), "journey around the moon" (R3), "swing around the moon" (R5), "journey to circle Earth and the moon" (R6), "around the Moon" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All describe the mission as going to/around the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "swing around, passing over the far side" ... "not entering low lunar orbit" ... "Apollo-era spacecraft, which orbited the moon" (R1), "pass around the Moon" ... "flying as close as ... from its surface" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: References specify a flyby, not orbit; explicitly contrasts with Apollo orbits.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will splash down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10" (R1), "splashdown" (R3), "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R5), "splash down in the Pacific Ocean ... on April 10" (R6), "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego ... April 10" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Exact location and date confirmed in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The goal of Artemis II is a crewed test flight to test the Orion spacecraft's systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey" ... "test flight" (R1), "Artemis II test flight" (R2), "test flight" ... "test Orion’s systems in their intended environment" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches descriptions of test objectives for Orion in deep space.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will travel around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "passing over the far side" ... "portions of the far side" (R1), "flyby of the lunar far side" (R3), "around the farside of the Moon" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states travel around/passing over the far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will become the first humans to travel around the far side of the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972." ... combined with far side travel descriptions
verifications.reasoning: R1 states Apollo 17 (1972) was last deep space trip; mission goes around far side, implying first since then. High confidence but indirect linkage.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will conclude with a high-speed splashdown on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "conclude with a splashdown ... on April 10" (R1), "splash down ... on April 10" (R6), "splashdown ... April 10" (R7); reentry at "40,000 kilometers per hour (25,000 miles per hour)" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Date and splashdown confirmed; 'high-speed' vaguely supported by reentry speeds but splashdown itself is low-speed after parachutes.
